h1: Which SEO company is best for your stage of business
metaTitle: Which SEO Company Is Best? Match by Stage
metaDescription: The best SEO company depends on your stage. Match a pre-revenue startup, a growing D2C brand, a local business and an enterprise site to the right team.
answer: The best SEO company is the one whose team shape matches your stage. A pre-revenue startup needs a consultant, not a retainer. A ₹5–25 crore D2C or SaaS brand needs a four-discipline team. A local service business needs map-pack work, not content. Enterprises need process and a migration specialist.
takeaways: "Best" is a matching problem, not a ranking problem. The agency that's excellent for a ₹20 crore brand is the wrong hire for a four-page local site.
Mismatches cost six months, not six weeks — because that's how long it takes for the wrong work to visibly fail.
Ask for two clients at your stage, not two famous logos. Logos tell you who could afford them.
The stage you're heading for matters less than the stage you're in. Buy for this year.

body: Every agency is best at something and mediocre at the rest. A shop that runs brilliant technical SEO for enterprise ecommerce will produce forgettable work for a dental clinic, and the boutique that dominates local map packs will drown in a 40,000-URL catalogue migration.

So stop asking which company is best and start asking which shape of team your business needs this year. If you want the vetting criteria rather than the stage map, we've published [a nine-point scorecard](/answers/what-is-the-best-seo-agency) separately. Here's the map.

body: At this stage SEO is usually the wrong channel and definitely the wrong retainer. You don't yet know which customers convert, and SEO takes three to six months to answer a question you can answer in three weeks with ₹50,000 of paid traffic.

What's genuinely worth buying is a few hours of a senior consultant: keyword and demand research to tell you whether the searches exist at all, a site structure that won't need rebuilding at 200 pages, and clean tracking from day one. Call it ₹25,000–₹60,000 as a one-off, then do the writing yourself. Founder-written content at this stage is usually better than agency content anyway, because you're the only one who's talked to the customers.
The failure mode here is a ₹40,000 retainer sold on a twelve-month contract. Twelve months of runway buys the wrong thing, and the agency will be honest about that only if their pipeline is full.

sections.h2: Local service business — one map pack, not a content plan
body: A clinic, a law firm, a salon, a packers-and-movers outfit. Your searches have a place attached, and most of the money sits in the map pack and on a handful of service-plus-city pages. Ninety per cent of the work is unglamorous and repeatable.

What you need is someone who will get the Google Business Profile categories and services right, build a real review flow into your operations, clean up citations where your name, address and phone disagree across directories, and write one solid page per service per city. That's it. It's largely done inside four months, after which the job becomes maintenance.

Which is why a ₹1,00,000 national retainer is a bad match here: they will sell you volume content because that's what fills a retainer, and volume content ranks for queries that don't call your reception. Look for a specialist at ₹25,000–₹60,000, or read [how local SEO actually works](/answers/how-to-do-local-seo) and run the first pass yourself.

sections.h2: ₹5–25 crore D2C or SaaS — the band where a real team pays for itself
body: This is the stage where a proper agency is genuinely the efficient choice. You have enough traffic for data to be meaningful, enough revenue that a 20% organic gain is a real number, and enough complexity that no single person can cover it. What the bands actually staff is set out in [what SEO costs in India](/cost/seo-cost-in-india).
You need all four disciplines running at once, which is the point most people miss when they compare quotes:
bullets: **Technical** — a catalogue or an app shell that Google can actually crawl and render, faceted navigation that doesn't generate 200,000 junk URLs, Core Web Vitals that don't cap everything else.
**Content** — comparison, category and bottom-of-funnel pages that match how people actually search when they're close to buying, not a blog calendar.
**Links and digital PR** — real placements, because at this stage your competitors have them and authority is the constraint.
**Analytics** — organic revenue by landing page, not sessions. Without it you'll be arguing about attribution instead of deciding anything.

callout.title: The quote that looks like a bargain
callout.body: At this stage you'll get quotes from ₹30,000 to ₹2,50,000 for what reads like the same scope. The cheap ones aren't cheaper agencies — they're a different product, staffed by one junior on a template. Compare named people and monthly output, never the summary line.

sections.h2: Enterprise and multi-brand — process beats brilliance
body: Above roughly ₹2,00,000 a month the constraint changes. It stops being SEO skill and starts being the ability to get anything shipped inside a company with a release train, a legal review and four stakeholders who each own part of the homepage.

The agency you want here has a project manager who is genuinely senior, has done migrations at your scale, can write a ticket a developer will accept without rewriting, and can survive a six-week approval cycle without losing the thread. Technical depth matters — log file analysis, faceted nav, hreflang across markets, staged rollouts — but coordination is what actually decides the outcome.
Boutiques that produce outstanding work for growth-stage clients often fail here, and it's not a talent problem. They're structured to move fast with one decision-maker, and there isn't one.

sections.h2: Why a mismatch costs six months, not six weeks
body: The reason stage-matching matters more in SEO than in paid media is the feedback loop. A bad ad campaign tells you it's bad in a fortnight. Bad SEO looks exactly like slow SEO — content shipping, reports arriving, rankings "building" — for months, because that's what correct work looks like too.

So the wrong-fit engagement runs its natural course. Three months of setup, two months of "give it time", one month of difficult conversations, and then a switch. You've spent the money, you've spent the time, and the new agency's first job is to undo some of it. That's the real cost of the mismatch, and it's why the cheap wrong choice is more expensive than the fair right one.
numbered: **Ask for two references at your stage and in your model.** Not the biggest logo — the closest match. A ₹50 crore client proves nothing about how they'd handle yours.
**Ask what they'd stop doing if your budget halved.** Their answer reveals what they think is actually driving the result versus what's filling the retainer.
**Ask which stage they're worst at.** Everyone has one. An agency that names theirs is telling you the truth about the other four answers too.

faqs.q: Which SEO company is best for a small business?
faqs.a: Usually a specialist or a good freelancer, not a general agency. Under about ₹40,000 a month an agency can only give you a fraction of one junior's week, while a specialist at the same price gives you a senior's focused attention on the two or three things that matter for your size.

faqs.q: Is a bigger SEO agency better?
faqs.a: No, it's just more insulated. Size buys process, bench strength and cover when someone leaves — genuinely useful at enterprise scale. It also means your account sits in a queue behind larger ones. Below roughly ₹1,50,000 a month, size mostly buys you a more polished pitch.

faqs.q: How do I compare SEO companies fairly?
faqs.a: Normalise the quotes first. Ask each for named people, hours per month, monthly output by deliverable, and where links come from. Then compare like with like. Comparing headline prices across proposals scoped differently is how the templated ₹30,000 option wins on paper.

faqs.q: What if I outgrow my SEO agency?
faqs.a: Common and not a failure. The agency that got you from 5,000 to 50,000 monthly sessions may not be built for migrations and multi-market work. Handle it honestly: give notice, get documentation and asset transfer in writing, and overlap by a month so context transfers rather than evaporates.

faqs.q: Which stage does Last Agency fit?
faqs.a: The ₹5–25 crore band, and local businesses that are serious about it. SEO starts at ₹75,000 a month, ₹40,000 for smaller sites, ex-GST. We take three clients a month because we freeze your trailing-90-day organic lead count and work free past 90 days if we haven't beaten it.
